title: A blocked reassign shows the status reason, reordering still works
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on the Work Orders build under test with Work Orders view permission and Work Orders create-and-edit; the Board View and Tech View display options are on.
  2. The current location has at least 3 lead technicians shown as groups/columns (a technician is eligible when they are Clockable, Active, and their role is not Office or Time Clock User).
  3. Via New Work Order, create several work orders and set a Lead Technician on each, spread across the technicians with some left Unassigned; then open the Work Orders page.
  4. A work order in a prohibited status; in Board/Tech View.
custom_steps:
1. Find the prohibited-status work order.
  2. Hover/open its disabled reassignment action and read the reason.
  3. Confirm it is visibly marked as not draggable.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The disabled Reassign lead technician action on an Invoiced or Paid work order shows the tooltip "The lead technician can't be changed once a work order is Invoiced or Paid."
  • The work order is shown as reorderable only within its current technician, not movable to another one.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043 (Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options). Story reference: SV-10047 — Reassign or unassign the lead technician. Spec: Confluence page 845185030 “Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options”, PRD v33 (2026-09-28), requirement(s) S4-N6, S4-N7 (read 30 Sep 2026). Review decisions/answers: Confluence page 853901313 where cited. Source-verified on 30 September 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S4-N6: “The disabled Reassign lead technician action on an Invoiced or Paid work order shows this tooltip: “The lead technician can’t be changed once a work order is Invoiced or Paid.””
  • S4-N7: “Visually indicate that an Invoiced or Paid work order can only be reordered within its current technician, not moved to another one.”
